ratings_why.fun: Borrow switching on before Full Moon triggers makes every neighbour a possible double, and choosing a shop phase versus a fight phase is a real decision each turn.
ratings_why.distinct: A windable shared clock plus text-borrowing from neighbours, the enemy and other tribes plays unlike any current tribe, though copy-a-neighbour has cousins elsewhere.

verdict_why: The engine is good; a few rules interactions (Waxwell against Once a turn, Grandam's copy stats) need wording before it can settle.

points.text: Dame Waxwell says triggers fire twice, but Sixpence Doe, The Moon-Scour and Grandam say Once a turn. Say whether the doubled firing gets past Once a turn; the answer decides her whole value.

Grandam's 'copy, keeping all stats the Leveret had gained' is ambiguous: copied base stats plus the Leveret's gains, or the Leveret's stats only? Also say whether a Leveret behind another Grandam copies Grandam.
Old Wat comes back every turn: say whether the returned Wat counts as Bought (1 gold a sale, forever) or Created (0).
Spring Jill is the only card with no hook into Borrow or the clock. Something a Borrower would want to lend, such as Moonlit Bristle that grows each Full, would give her a combo use.
Waning has one card. A Waning payoff that a Jack or Leveret can borrow would make the whole cycle worth steering, not just Full and New.

standouts.why: Ribboned Jack doubles a neighbour's Full Moon trigger, a Pass unit, Pack or Longshanks' bout: one card, many off-label uses.
Grandam turning a grown back row into copies of the Hares in front, which can then triple, is the best combo payoff here.
The Three Hares beside Dusk Nurse's targets or a Charmer spreads every permanent gain sideways into Leverets: a quiet engine the builds don't even list.

weakest.why: Spring Jill is a vanilla body with Moonlit Bristle; nothing else in the tribe cares about her.
Moon-Caller's death turn is clever but often switches Moonlit off by stepping Full to Waning; it is narrow.
Sixpence Doe is a plain gold trigger; fine, but no interplay beyond Waxwell.

flags.note: Grandam copies count towards triples and each triple Discovers; with Waxwell this can run away.
Silverpenny borrows always, not only under the Full moon, so she doubles another tribe's capstone every fight from Tier 5.
Doubling versus Once a turn on other cards is not settled.
Which stats a Leveret keeps when it becomes a copy is not clear.
Witch borrows the enemy across, but in the shop there is no enemy; say it works only in fights.
